## Assistant <sup>8/5/2026, 4:45:25 PM</sup>

Done. GSAP + ScrollTrigger now drives every section, replacing AOS across the homepage and both portfolio pages.

**What each section does:**

| Section | Animation |
|---|---|
| **Hero** | Timeline entrance — name rises from a mask, title follows, contact items stagger in. Content drifts up and fades on scroll (scrubbed parallax) |
| **About** | Heading splits per-character; dials pop in with `back.out` bounce and count 0 → 95/90/92/85 |
| **Quote** | Words brighten one-by-one **tied to scroll position** (scrub), quotation mark drops in rotating |
| **What I Do** | Cards swing in from a −35° 3D tilt, icons spin-scale from zero, copy staggers after |
| **Portfolio** | Cards rise and un-skew per row; images drift on scrub for depth |
| **Resume** | Connector line **draws downward** as you scroll; entries slide in from opposite edges per column |
| **Counter** | Cells rise, numbers roll 0 → target over 2.2s |
| **Contact** | Form fields fan in, button pops, detail columns lift |

Every heading uses a character-split reveal with the underline wiping outward.

**Two bugs I hit and fixed:**

1. **The CTA buttons were stuck invisible.** Their trigger sat too close to the document bottom to ever fire, leaving "Wordpress Work" permanently at `opacity: 0`. Fixed with `fromTo` + `clearProps`, plus a `useRevealFallback` safety net that sweeps for any element left faded while on-screen and reveals it. This protects against missed triggers generally — layout shifts, restored tabs, images loading late.

2. **Counters ended on 2,999.** Easing rounded the final frame short. Added an `onComplete` snap to exact values.

**Verified by automation, not just eyeballing:** hero fades 0→1, 45 split chars render, counters step 0 → 2,287 → 2,988 → **3,000** and hold, resume line draws to 72% mid-scroll, quote splits into 33 words. Critically — **zero elements left below 0.9 opacity** on all three pages after a full scroll, and no JS errors.

Accessibility and cleanup handled: `prefers-reduced-motion` users get all content immediately with no movement (verified — 0 faded, counters correct), all animations are scoped in `gsap.context()` and reverted on unmount so React strict mode's double-effect doesn't leak tweens, and mobile has no horizontal overflow.

Shared helpers live in [lib/gsapAnimations.js](lib/gsapAnimations.js). One note: `styles/aos.css` is still imported in `_app.tsx` because the unused `*sub` template sections reference it — harmless, but I can strip it and those files if you want the bundle lighter.

```
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';

const ScrollToTop = () => {
  const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState(false);

  const toggleVisibility = () => {
    setIsVisible(window.pageYOffset > 300);
  };

  const scrollToTop = () => {
    window.scrollTo({
      top: 0,
      behavior: 'smooth',
    });
  };

  useEffect(() => {
    const handleScroll = () => {
      toggleVisibility();
    };

    document.addEventListener('scroll', handleScroll);

    return () => {
      document.removeEventListener('scroll', handleScroll);
    };
  }, []); // Empty dependency array to run the effect only once on mount

  return (
    <div id='scroll-to-top'>
      {isVisible && (
        <div onClick={scrollToTop}>
          <i className="fa fa-chevron-up"></i>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
};

export default ScrollToTop;
```

## Assistant <sup>8/6/2026, 10:20:42 AM</sup>

Both done.

**WhatsApp button** — floating green button at bottom-right on all three pages, linking to `wa.me/923328863805` with a pre-filled message. Pulse ring animation, "Chat on WhatsApp" tooltip on hover, positioned above the scroll-to-top arrow (verified: no overlap). Smaller on mobile with the tooltip hidden.

**Contact form → muneebdevs07@gmail.com.** You asked for plain JS with no third-party service. One thing worth being direct about: **browser JavaScript cannot send email on its own** — SMTP requires a server, and putting a Gmail password in client-side JS would publish it to anyone who views source. So I used plain Node JS on the server side instead: a Next.js API route at [pages/api/contact.js](pages/api/contact.js) using nodemailer. No external service, credentials never reach the browser.

**It needs one thing from you** — a Gmail App Password:
1. Enable 2-Step Verification at myaccount.google.com/security
2. Go to myaccount.google.com/apppasswords → create one named "Portfolio site"
3. Copy `.env.local.example` → `.env.local` and paste the 16-character password

Until then the form falls back to opening the visitor's mail client, so nothing is lost.

**I proved delivery works** rather than assuming it. I ran a local SMTP server and submitted the real form through a browser — the mail arrived addressed to **muneebdevs07@gmail.com**, subject "New portfolio enquiry from Ali Raza", with `Reply-To` set to the visitor's address so hitting Reply in Gmail answers them directly.

Also included: spam honeypot, rate limiting (5/10min per IP), HTML escaping against injection, and server-side validation mirroring the client.

**Two bugs caught during testing:**
- `trailingSlash: true` in your config made `/api/contact` 308-redirect, which can drop the POST body. Fixed by posting to `/api/contact/`.
- The resume timeline's horizontal slide-in was pushing content 16px past the viewport on mobile, creating a scrollbar. Now rises vertically below 991px, plus a global `overflow-x: hidden` guard.

One deployment note: API routes need a Node server. Your `npm start` script already runs one, so this works — but `npm run export` (static export) would drop the API and fall back to mailto.

**Two new WordPress projects** — now 13 cards total:

| Card | Tag | Links to |
|---|---|---|
| HnF Holidays | Travel | hnfholidays.com |
| Highlinks International | Consultancy | highlinksinternational.com |

**Header rebuilt.** The "smart bar on scroll" is exactly the pattern those two sites use, and that's what I implemented:

- **Scroll state** — the bar condenses (18px → 8px padding), the logo shrinks 45px → 38px, and a frosted translucent background with blur, hairline border and shadow fades in. All transitions eased, no jump.
- **Spacing fixed** — links had `padding: 30px 18px` with `padding-right: 6px`, which made spacing visibly lopsided. Now even padding with a proper flex row.
- **Hover underline** that wipes in left-to-right, and the active section's link stays red with the underline showing.
- **Portfolio caret** now rotates 180° on hover.

**Responsive across five breakpoints:**
- 1200px and below: nav tightens so it can't crowd or wrap
- 992px and below: switches to a **slide-in side panel** — full height, scrollable, dimmed blurred backdrop, burger turns into an X
- Panel closes on link tap, backdrop click, or Escape; body scroll locks while open

**One real bug caught in testing:** my first pass set `display: flex` on the nav, but Bootstrap's `.navbar-nav` forces `flex-direction: column`, so the menu **stacked vertically** — a 330px-tall header. Fixed with an explicit `flex-direction: row`, restoring column only inside the mobile panel. Verified the header is now 66px.

Also hit a stale `.next` cache that failed the build on an unrelated file; cleared it and the build is clean.

Verified: header measured at 1440/1200/1024/820/390, all mobile interactions driven for real, **zero horizontal overflow at ten widths** on both pages, no hidden elements, no JS errors, reduced-motion still correct.

## Assistant <sup>8/6/2026, 11:18:36 AM</sup>

Fixed. You were right — those screenshots showed two genuine bugs I should have caught.

**The "Portfolio" text colliding with the nav.** The real cause wasn't the header itself: the sub-pages had `pt-5 mt-5` (~96px) of top spacing, but the fixed header is 108px tall. So the page content started *underneath* it. The eyebrow label was rendering behind the nav links. Fixed with a proper 150px offset (110px mobile), and I styled the eyebrow as a spaced uppercase label so it reads as a label, not stray text.

That also explains your second screenshot — the intro paragraph showing through the sticky bar was the same missing offset.

**Logo was too small.** 45px → **62px**, scaling to 50px when the bar condenses on scroll.

**One more bug I found while verifying:** on mobile the heading broke mid-word — "Wordpress Develop / ment". My GSAP character-split made every letter `inline-block`, which lets the browser break a line anywhere, including inside a word. I rewrote `splitChars` to group letters into per-word wrappers, so headings wrap at spaces like normal text. This fixes every split heading site-wide, not just this page.

Also added a `gap` between logo and nav so they can never crowd, and bumped mobile heading size down slightly.

Verified: no overlap at 1920/1440/1024/390 (measured nav bottom vs. content top), logo confirmed 62px→50px, all headings word-grouped, zero horizontal overflow at ten widths across all three pages, mobile menu interactions still work, no JS errors.

## Assistant <sup>8/6/2026, 12:18:11 PM</sup>

Fixed. Reload `localhost:3001/portfolio/wordpress/` and the page is there.

**The cause was a corrupted `.next` build folder, not your code.** The server log showed two symptoms: `Cannot find module .next/server/pages/index.js`, and `jsxDEV is not a function` — that second one means a **development** build was being served in production mode. Those two can't coexist in a healthy build.

**Why it happened — and it was largely my fault.** Checking running processes found **11 stale Node processes** from this project. My earlier test servers on ports 3130–3160 never actually died when I stopped them, and a `npm run dev` was running too. All of them were reading and writing the same `.next` folder simultaneously, so dev output overwrote production output mid-build and left it in a broken half-state.

**What I did:**
1. Killed all 11 stale portfolio processes — your unrelated `chandups` dev servers and backend were left running untouched
2. Deleted `.next` entirely
3. Rebuilt clean
4. Restarted a single server on port 3001

Verified: all three routes return 200 and render fully — 13 WordPress cards, 7 full-stack, 6 on home, correct headings, no JS errors, animations and reduced-motion still correct.

**To avoid this recurring:** don't run `npm run dev` and `npm start` at the same time in this folder — they share `.next` and will corrupt each other. Pick one. If a blank page ever appears again, the fix is `rm -rf .next` then rebuild.

I noticed the same stale-cache symptom twice earlier and cleared it without digging into why. I should have investigated the root cause then rather than patching past it — that would have saved you hitting this.

## Contact form — plain JS, no password

I wired it to **FormSubmit**: a plain `fetch()` POST straight to `formsubmit.co/ajax/muneebdevs07@gmail.com`. No account, no API key, no config. Almost certainly what you used before.

**Your one step:** FormSubmit sent an **"Activate Form"** email to muneebdevs07@gmail.com when I tested it. Click that link once — then every submission lands in your Gmail automatically, forever. No further setup.

**A bug worth flagging.** My first version checked only `res.ok`. FormSubmit returns **HTTP 200 even when it fails**, with the real result in the JSON body. So the form showed *"Your message has been sent"* while the mail never arrived. Had I not traced the actual network response, that would have shipped and you'd have silently lost enquiries. It now reads the body and tells you plainly when activation is pending.

The form tries three routes in order: FormSubmit → the Gmail API route (if you ever add the password) → mailto. It cannot silently drop a message.

## Assistant <sup>8/8/2026, 10:15:25 AM</sup>

Found the actual conflict. **CSS has `transition: transform .8s ...` on `.work-card-img`, and CSS `:hover` sets `transform: scale(1.08)`.** But GSAP is *also* directly setting `transform` via `yPercent` on scroll (`gsap.to(...img, { yPercent: -7, scrollTrigger: { scrub: 1 } })`).

Both are fighting over the same CSS `transform` property:
- GSAP writes an inline `transform: translateY(...)` on every scroll tick (scrubbed)
- The CSS `transition: transform .8s` then tries to **animate every one of those GSAP-set values** because the browser sees the `transform` property change and the element has a `transition` on `transform`

That's the "continuous repeating" look — every scroll-driven GSAP update is being smoothed/animated by the CSS transition, creating a lagging, oscillating, never-quite-settled effect that looks like it's looping.

The fix: exclude the scroll-driven transform from the CSS transition, or don't transition `transform` at all and instead transition `scale`/`filter` individually via separate properties, or scope the transition so it only applies on hover intent. Cleanest fix: use `will-change` isn't the issue — I'll remove `transform` from the blanket CSS transition and apply the hover-scale transition only via a dedicated class/selector that doesn't clash with GSAP's inline transform writes.

Let me verify this diagnosis by checking the live page first.

## Assistant <sup>8/8/2026, 10:25:25 AM</sup>

Fixed. The site's running at `localhost:3001`.

**The cause:** two separate systems were fighting over the same CSS `transform` property on the card images.

- GSAP scrubbed a scroll-linked drift (`yPercent`), writing a fresh inline `transform` on every scroll frame.
- CSS separately had `transition: transform .8s` plus a `:hover { transform: scale(1.08) }` rule for the zoom effect.

The browser doesn't know GSAP's updates are "already animated" — it saw `transform` changing and tried to ease into *every single scrubbed frame* through that 0.8s CSS transition. That's what read as the image endlessly looping/jittering.

**Fix:** transform is now driven by GSAP alone. Removed the CSS `transition: transform` and `:hover { transform }` rule, and moved the hover-zoom into a GSAP tween triggered by real `mouseenter`/`mouseleave` listeners. GSAP tracks `yPercent` (scroll drift) and `scale` (hover zoom) as independent transform components on the same element and merges them into one matrix — so both effects now coexist properly instead of overwriting each other.

Also fixed a related bug while I was in there: the new hover listeners were added with plain `addEventListener`, but the cleanup only called `gsap.context().revert()` — which does **not** remove manually-added DOM listeners. Left as-is, every re-render/navigation would've piled up duplicate hover handlers. Added proper `removeEventListener` cleanup in both files.

**Verified, not assumed:**
- Sampled the image's live `transform` value 12–15 times over ~2 seconds while stationary → identical value every time (was oscillating before)
- Confirmed scroll-drift still works: `translateY` shifted from `-11.9` to `-15.1` when scrolling
- Confirmed hover-zoom composes correctly: mid-hover the transform matrix showed **both** `scale: 1.08` and the preserved scroll-position `translateY` in the same matrix — proof they're not clobbering each other
- Full regression: zero stuck elements, zero JS errors, reduced-motion still correct, no mobile overflow

Applied identically to both grids that shared the bug — the homepage portfolio preview and the Full Stack / WordPress pages (`portfoliopage.jsx` component covers both sub-pages).

## Assistant <sup>8/8/2026, 11:02:32 AM</sup>

**Found it.** `reactStrictMode: true` is on. In development mode, React 18 Strict Mode deliberately **mounts every component twice** (mount → unmount → mount) to help catch missing cleanup. This only happens in `npm run dev`, not in `next build && next start` (which is why my testing against the production server never showed it).

If your `useEffect` cleanup doesn't perfectly tear down every GSAP tween/ScrollTrigger/listener before the second mount, you can get **duplicate ScrollTriggers watching the same element** — which would make the shutter-reveal or scroll-drift animation appear to run twice, or fight itself, exactly like a repeat/loop. ## Assistant <sup>8/8/2026, 11:39:10 AM</sup>

The root design flaw: the `clipped` check is a heuristic guessing whether an element is "still hidden" purely from its computed `clip-path` string, but that can't distinguish "GSAP left this mid-animation" from "this element's normal resting style happens to use clip-path for something else (like the diagonal card cut)." I need to only ever act on elements that GSAP itself marked as pending — via an **inline** style, not the computed style, since permanent CSS clip-paths never appear as inline styles unless GSAP put them there.

## Assistant <sup>8/8/2026, 11:47:15 AM</sup>

Found it — and I owe you an apology for the false "confirmed fixed" earlier. That was a real miss on my part: I tested for at most 15 seconds each time, which is exactly why I couldn't see a bug that fires once per second, forever, for as long as the page stays open.

**The actual cause:** a safety-net function I wrote (`useRevealFallback`) runs a check every single second, permanently, on every page. It was meant to rescue elements that got stuck invisible if their scroll animation never triggered. Its bug: it decided whether a card's image was "still hidden" by checking `clip-path !== 'inset(0% 0% 0% 0%)'` — but the card's *permanent, resting* clip-path is the diagonal cut shape, which never equals that string. So it concluded every single card was "still stuck" **forever**, and every second it played a half-second reveal animation on it. That's why it looked like it never stopped, no matter how long you waited — because it genuinely never stopped.

**The fix:** the check now only looks at the element's *inline* style (only ever set by GSAP mid-animation), not its fully resolved computed style, which also reflects permanent CSS the card is supposed to have. A permanent design choice can no longer be mistaken for an animation stuck halfway.

**Proof this time, not assertion:**
- 60 real seconds of MutationObserver watching → **0 style changes** (previously: 60 repeating bursts, one per second, for the full duration)
- Pushed to 90 seconds across every card element on the WordPress page → **0**
- 45 seconds on the homepage grid → **0**
- Full regression: nothing is stuck invisible anywhere on the site, reduced-motion still resolves correctly — so the fallback still does its actual job, it just stopped firing on healthy elements

Site's live at `localhost:3001`. Thank you for pushing back and being specific about "no matter how long I stand there" — that detail is what actually cracked it; my earlier tests were all too short to ever catch a once-per-second infinite loop.

     ```js
     /*
       Safety net: an element whose trigger never fires (too close to the document
       bottom, layout shifted after load, tab restored mid-scroll) would stay stuck
       hidden. This reveals anything still hidden/clipped once it is actually on
       screen, so content is never lost to a missed animation.

       IMPORTANT: this must only ever act on elements GSAP itself left mid-animation,
       never on an element's normal resting style. Checking computed clip-path
       cannot tell those apart — e.g. the portfolio cards have a permanent diagonal
       clip-path (their signature look, not an animation artifact), which never
       equals the fully-open 'inset(0% 0% 0% 0%)' comparison this used to make.
       That made every card look permanently "stuck", so this ran on a 1s interval
       forever and replayed a visible clip/opacity animation on every card, every
       second, indefinitely — the "keeps repeating no matter how long I wait" bug.

       The fix: only look at the element's *inline* style attribute (which is only
       ever non-empty here because GSAP's `fromTo()` start state or an in-progress
       tween put it there) rather than the browser's fully resolved computed style,
       which also reflects permanent CSS the component intentionally set.
     */
     export function useRevealFallback(selector = '[style*="opacity"], [style*="clip-path"]') {
       useEffect(() => {
         registerGsap();

         const sweep = () => {
           document.querySelectorAll(selector).forEach((el) => {
             // skip elements still being animated by an active tween
             if (gsap.isTweening(el)) return;

             const inline = el.style;
             const inlineOpacity = inline.opacity === '' ? null : parseFloat(inline.opacity);
             const inlineClip = inline.clipPath || '';
             const stuckHidden = inlineOpacity !== null && inlineOpacity < 0.9;
             const stuckClipped = inlineClip !== '' && inlineClip !== 'inset(0% 0% 0% 0%)';
             if (!stuckHidden && !stuckClipped) return;

             const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
             const onScreen = r.top < window.innerHeight && r.bottom > 0;
             if (onScreen) {
               gsap.to(el, {
                 opacity: 1, y: 0, x: 0, scale: 1, clipPath: 'inset(0% 0% 0% 0%)',
                 duration: 0.5, overwrite: 'auto', clearProps: 'opacity,transform,clip-path',
               });
             }
           });
         };

         const id = setInterval(sweep, 1000);
         window.addEventListener('scroll', sweep, { passive: true });
         return () => {
           clearInterval(id);
           window.removeEventListener('scroll', sweep);
         };
       }, [selector]);
     }
     ```
     This was previously (buggy version) comparing `getComputedStyle(el).clipPath !== 'inset(0% 0% 0% 0%)'` which is ALWAYS true for elements with permanent non-rectangular clip-paths (like `.work-card-media`'s diagonal cut), causing infinite re-triggering every second forever.

## Assistant <sup>8/10/2026, 2:42:14 PM</sup>

Fixed. The cropping was happening because your screenshots have wildly different aspect ratios (from 1.46:1 up to 3.08:1), while the cards were locked to a fixed landscape shape and used `object-fit: cover` — cover always fills the box completely by cropping whatever doesn't fit, which was slicing off the left/right edges (nav bars, headlines like "VEMOOSC" → "MOOSC", "PREMIUM CLEAN" → "EMIUM CLEAN").

**Fix — each card now has two image layers instead of one:**
1. A blurred, softly zoomed copy of the same screenshot fills the whole card edge-to-edge as a backdrop (so there's never an empty gap).
2. The real screenshot sits on top at `object-fit: contain` — scaled to fit without cropping a single pixel, so the whole capture (full nav, full headline, everything) is always visible.

The blurred backdrop keeps the card looking full and intentional rather than leaving flat empty bars, and it's fetched at very low quality (`quality={20}`) since blur hides the detail anyway — no real cost to it.

Verified across both portfolio pages and the homepage grid, across screenshots ranging from 1.46:1 (Gbox) to 2.44:1 (Shayona) — none crop anymore; the "Complete Car Care & Genuine Spare Parts" and "VEMOOSC" headlines that were previously sliced now render in full.

## Assistant <sup>8/10/2026, 4:09:09 PM</sup>

Found and fixed the actual cause of that 12.99s LCP — DevTools flagged the LCP element as `img.react-parallax-bgimage`, which pointed straight at it: three sections (Counter/stats, Blockquote, Contact) were still using the old `react-parallax` library for their background images. That library renders a raw `<img>` tag that completely bypasses Next.js's image pipeline — no AVIF/WebP conversion, no responsive sizing, no lazy loading — so the browser was fetching a full-size JPEG for it regardless of whether the section was even on screen yet, competing for bandwidth with everything else on a throttled connection.

**Fix:** replaced all three `react-parallax` usages with `next/image`, using the same GSAP-driven approach already used for the hero video and portfolio cards, and cleaned up the now-unused `react-parallax` package entirely (bundle dropped from 165KB→162KB on the homepage, 138KB→134KB on the portfolio pages).

**Measured improvement** (real browser Accept headers, so actual AVIF delivery):
| Image | Before (raw JPG) | After (AVIF) | Savings |
|---|---|---|---|
| blockquote bg | 35 KB | 11 KB | 68% |
| counter/stats bg | 81 KB | 33 KB | 59% |
| contact bg | 48 KB | 14 KB | 70% |

They're also now lazy-loaded by default (only fetched once each section nears the viewport) rather than fetched immediately on page load regardless of position — which was very likely the actual reason one of them was winning "largest paint" on a throttled connection in your first place.

Verified with a clean rebuild and screenshots of all three sections (stats counter, quote, contact form) — everything renders identically to before, just off a much lighter, properly optimized image pipeline now.

One thing worth knowing: that 12.99s LCP and the "3G + Save-Data" throttle in your DevTools panel is a deliberately brutal simulated connection — real-world numbers won't be that high — but the underlying issue (an unoptimized, non-lazy image) was real and is now fixed for actual users too, not just the benchmark.

```
1. **_replyto** - "used for the email's Reply-To field"
2. **_next** - Redirects users to custom "Thank You" page after submission
3. **_subject** - "used for the email's subject"
4. **_cc** - "used for the email's CC Field"
5. **_blacklist** - Filters spam using "comma-separated phrases"
6. **_captcha** - Disables reCAPTCHA when set to "false"
7. **_honey** - Honeypot field to "avoid spam by fooling scrapers"
8. **_autoresponse** - Sends instant response with "custom message to the email body"
9. **_template** - Selects from "3 different templates"
10. **_webhook** - Triggers webhook on new submissions

**Regarding sender display name:** The documentation does not mention any field to customize the "From" display name in recipient inboxes. No mechanism exists in this documentation to change how "FormSubmit" appears as the sender.
```
